description: Omitting the chest pocket entirely produces the cleanest, most austere front on a jacket, erasing any visual interruption across the chest. Historically associated with tailcoats and the most elevated forms of formalwear, it was considered the hallmark of true ceremonial dress. In modern bespoke tailoring it is chosen on double-breasted dinner suits or highly formal morning coats where a boutonnière replaces the pocket square as the only chest ornament.
